title: Adverbs: how and how often
goal: Put adverbs like always, only and well in the right place
intro: Adverbs tell us how, when, where or how often. Most “how” adverbs end in -ly (quickly, carefully), but “good” becomes “well”. Frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, never) go before the main verb but after “be”. And “only” should sit right next to the word it limits.

rules.rule: Frequency: before the main verb, after am/is/are.

examples: She is a good speaker. She speaks well.

rules.rule: Put “only” next to what it limits.
examples: I only have 100 rupees. / I have only 100 rupees.

rules.rule: hard and fast have no -ly. “Hardly” means almost not.
examples: I hardly slept. (I slept very little.)

mistakes.why: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb.
Using “only” for emphasis like this is Indian English; just drop it.

ex.q: My brother ___ calls me on Sundays.
He is ___ at home in the evening.
I ___ know him. We met once.
Sometimes she is working from home.
You did very good in the interview.
ex.fixed: You did very well in the interview.

ex.q: We go often to that café.
ex.fixed: We often go to that café.

ex.q: I ___ eat meat. I’m vegetarian. (always / never)

ex.a: She has never been late for work.

ex.q: Correct this: “Always I am forgetting my keys.”
a: I am always forgetting my keys

talk: Talk about your habits: what you always, usually, sometimes and never do, and one thing you do really well.
